title: Project Pluto
summary: A US program (1957–1964) to build a nuclear-ramjet-powered cruise missile that would fly at Mach 3 at treetop level, delivering warheads across the Soviet Union while spewing lethal reactor exhaust. The weapon was so indiscriminately destructive — killing populations along its own flight path — that it was cancelled without ever flying a complete mission profile.

facts.label: Engine tested
facts.value: Tory-IIA (1961) and Tory-IIC (1964), Nevada Test Site

facts.label: Warhead capacity
facts.value: Up to 16 thermonuclear bombs in a single pass

facts.label: Cancellation date
facts.value: July 1, 1964 — ICBMs deemed less indiscriminate and more controllable
